# STUDENT DRESS CODE AND UNIFORM POLICY

## 1. Purpose and General Guidelines
The school uniform promotes equality, discipline, and a sense of belonging among students. All students from Grades 1 to 12 are expected to arrive on campus in neat, clean, and properly pressed uniforms every working day.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

45fac962-16b7-4515-8d0e-ff03e926474d.text:
## 2. Regular Academic Days (Monday to Thursday)
- **Boys (Grades 1–5):** Navy blue half-sleeve shorts, crisp white collared shirt with school monogram on the pocket, navy blue belt with school emblem, black velcro/lace leather shoes, and navy blue cotton socks.
- **Boys (Grades 6–12):** Navy blue formal trousers, crisp white full-sleeve or half-sleeve collared shirt, school striped tie, navy blue belt, black formal leather shoes, and navy blue socks.
- **Girls (Grades 1–5):** Navy blue pleated tunic, crisp white collared blouse, school tie, black buckle shoes, and navy blue socks.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

2b53a2f2-140a-4f75-8a32-42cf3dc51a74.text: - **Girls (Grades 6–12):** Navy blue divided skirt (knee-length) or formal trousers, crisp white collared shirt, school striped tie, black formal shoes, and navy blue socks.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

c53f62bf-b997-4f69-aa25-1a5ff1c7d45d.text:
## 3. Sports and House Activity Days (Friday and Saturday)
Students must wear their assigned House uniform based on their house allocation (Red House, Blue House, Green House, or Yellow House):
- **Top:** Breathable House-colored polo T-shirt with the school crest.
- **Bottom:** White track pants with dual navy side stripes.
- **Footwear:** Pure white canvas or running sports shoes with white socks.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

9cad56fd-e0e9-46e1-a1b5-3f8b8ff8c92a.text:
## 4. Winter Uniform Guidelines (November 1 to February 28)
- **Grades 1–5:** Navy blue V-neck knitted sleeveless or full-sleeve sweater with the school crest.
- **Grades 6–12:** Navy blue tailored blazer with brass buttons and the official school crest is mandatory during morning assembly and formal school events. Navy blue woolen caps and mufflers are permitted during extreme cold weather.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

222decf8-ca84-4c83-8e05-a6671723eb4a.text:
## 5. Personal Grooming and Accessories
- **ID Card:** The laminated School Identity Card with the current academic year lanyard must be worn around the neck at all times on campus and on the school bus.
- **Hair & Nails:** Boys must maintain a short, neat haircut. Girls with shoulder-length or longer hair must tie it neatly into two braids or a ponytail using navy blue or black hairbands. Nails must be trimmed short and kept free of nail polish.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

c2e3ad94-c63c-4386-9952-51ade508f491.text: - **Prohibited Items:** Smartwatches, fitness bands, gold/expensive jewelry, mehendi/tattoos, and colored contact lenses are strictly prohibited. Only simple analog wristwatches are allowed from Grade 6 onward.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

879e62c1-d41f-4981-bd91-837177e5d70f.text:
## 6. Non-Compliance Policy
- First violation: Written remark in the Student Almanac/Diary.
- Three consecutive violations: Parents will be notified by the Discipline Coordinator, and the student may not be permitted to attend regular classes until the uniform requirement is met.

metadata.title: Student Dress Code and Uniform Policy

c8d3aade-05c6-4ebb-a956-806ad048a7c7.text:
# ANNUAL FEE STRUCTURE, PAYMENT SCHEDULE, AND SCHOLARSHIPS

## 1. One-Time Admission Charges (New Students Only)
- **Registration & Prospectus Fee:** ₹1,000 (non-refundable, payable at the time of application).
- **Admission Fee:** ₹15,000 (one-time, non-refundable upon confirmation of seat).
- **Caution Money (Security Deposit):** ₹5,000 (refundable upon withdrawal from the school after clearing all library, laboratory, and transport dues).

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

57e72596-7397-45d6-b63b-763b686423b1.text:
## 2. Quarterly Tuition and Composite Fee Structure (2026–2027)
Fees are billed on a quarterly basis (4 quarters per academic year):
- **Primary Wing (Grades 1 to 5):** ₹13,500 per quarter (₹4,500/month).
- **Middle Wing (Grades 6 to 8):** ₹16,500 per quarter (₹5,500/month).
- **Secondary Wing (Grades 9 & 10):** ₹18,000 per quarter (₹6,000/month).
- **Senior Secondary Wing – Commerce & Humanities (Grades 11 & 12):** ₹20,400 per quarter (₹6,800/month).
- **Senior Secondary Wing – Science with Lab (Grades 11 & 12):** ₹22,500 per quarter (₹7,500/month).

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

8115a1a0-0d17-489a-a901-3aafde753753.text:
## 3. Annual Activity and Technology Charges
Payable once per year along with Quarter 1 fees:
- **Smart Class, ERP Portal & Library Fee:** ₹4,500 per year.
- **Sports, Arts & Annual Event Fee:** ₹3,500 per year.

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

0463c785-54b9-48bb-a8b2-7102290684fd.text:
## 4. Quarterly Payment Deadlines and Late Penalties
- **Quarter 1 (April–June):** Due by April 10, 2026.
- **Quarter 2 (July–September):** Due by July 10, 2026.
- **Quarter 3 (October–December):** Due by October 10, 2026.
- **Quarter 4 (January–March):** Due by January 10, 2027.
- **Late Fee Penalty:** A grace period is provided until the 15th of the due month. From the 16th onward, a late fine of ₹50 per day is automatically charged by the ERP system. If fees remain unpaid for over 45 days, the student's name may be struck off the rolls.

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

434fa6a9-8dcb-4bf5-89c4-8ddb66a29094.text:
## 5. Accepted Payment Modes
- Online via the School Parent Portal (UPI, Net Banking, Debit/Credit Cards) with zero convenience fee on UPI.
- Demand Draft (DD) or Account Payee Cheque drawn in favor of "Greenwood International School" submitted at the Accounts Counter (9:00 AM to 2:00 PM, Monday to Friday). Cash payments above ₹2,000 are not accepted.

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

40249906-48ca-4a5c-832f-da157e0e0441.text:
## 6. Fee Concessions and Merit Scholarships
- **Sibling Concession:** A 15% discount on the quarterly tuition fee is granted to the younger sibling studying concurrently in the school.
- **Merit Scholarship (Grades 9–12):** Students scoring 95% and above in the annual school examination or CBSE Board examination receive a 50% tuition fee waiver for the following academic year.
- **Sports Excellence Waiver:** National-level medalists representing the school receive a 25% tuition fee concession upon approval by the Principal.

metadata.title: Annual Fee Structure, Payment Schedule, and Scholarships

54935a48-e768-4da4-8dd2-4e508ba75a2c.text:
# SCHOOL TIMINGS, ATTENDANCE RULES, AND LEAVE POLICY

## 1. Seasonal School Timings
The school follows two seasonal schedules to ensure student comfort:
- **Summer Schedule (April 1 to October 31):**
  - Reporting Time: 7:45 AM
  - Morning Assembly: 7:50 AM to 8:05 AM
  - Gate Closure: 7:55 AM sharp
  - Dismissal (Grades 1–5): 1:15 PM
  - Dismissal (Grades 6–12): 1:45 PM
- **Winter Schedule (November 1 to March 31):**
  - Reporting Time: 8:15 AM
  - Morning Assembly: 8:20 AM to 8:35 AM
  - Gate Closure: 8:25 AM sharp
  - Dismissal (Grades 1–5): 1:45 PM
  - Dismissal (Grades 6–12): 2:15 PM

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

35faa1e8-0804-44de-aaf1-5301bb03e15d.text:
## 2. Late Arrival Policy
- Students arriving after gate closure will be marked "Late" in the attendance register.
- Three late arrivals in a single calendar month will result in a written warning to parents. On the fourth late arrival, the student will be sent back home with the parent/guardian.

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

d43d4dc5-589a-42dc-ab38-eb2c9243c960.text:
## 3. Mandatory Attendance Requirements
- A minimum of **75% attendance** across the academic session is compulsory for every student to be eligible to appear in the Final Term-End Examinations.
- Students with attendance below 75% will only be considered for examination eligibility in cases of severe hospitalization, supported by complete hospital discharge summaries and approved by the Principal.

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

934fb7ac-46d0-41c2-8104-85c28ee12c74.text:
## 4. Leave Application Procedure
- **Planned Leave (1–2 Days):** Parents must submit a prior leave request via the Parent Mobile App or the Leave Record section of the Student Almanac at least 24 hours in advance.
- **Medical Leave (3 or More Days):** A formal application accompanied by a prescription and fitness certificate from a registered medical practitioner (MBBS or above) must be submitted to the Class Teacher on the day the student resumes school.

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

0d945604-fd52-4d85-9197-ac49392d9bca.text: - **Uninformed Absence:** Continuous absence for 10 working days without written intimation will result in automatic removal of the student's name from the school register.

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

02e1e52c-5451-4b16-bbda-115f55f5c362.text:
## 5. Early Dispersal and Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTM)
- **Early Dispersal:** Students are not permitted to leave school early during working hours unless collected in person by a parent/authorized guardian carrying the Parent Escort Card, following approval from the Wing Coordinator.
- **Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTM):** Conducted on the last Saturday of every month from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM. Attendance by at least one parent is mandatory to review academic progress.

metadata.title: School Timings, Attendance Rules, and Leave Policy

12516502-29b2-4dc5-8123-1b293278c689.text:
# EXAMINATION FRAMEWORK, ASSESSMENT PATTERN, AND PROMOTION RULES

## 1. Academic Calendar and Term Structure
The academic year runs from April to March and is divided into two semesters:
- **Term 1:** April to September (culminating in Half-Yearly Examinations in September).
- **Term 2:** October to March (culminating in Annual Examinations in February/March).

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

de2c96a5-63d7-4091-88ee-c4201530ceae.text:
## 2. Assessment Weightage (Grades 6 to 10)
Each term carries 100 marks per subject, distributed as follows:
- **Periodic Assessment (20 Marks):** Best two out of three Periodic Tests (10 marks), Notebook Submission & Maintenance (5 marks), and Subject Enrichment / Lab Activity (5 marks).
- **Term-End Written Examination (80 Marks):** Comprehensive 3-hour written exam covering the prescribed term syllabus.

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

5e49d2ac-561e-46f0-af5f-be337cc38f43.text:
## 3. Assessment Weightage (Senior Secondary – Grades 11 & 12)
- **Subjects with Practicals (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Physical Education):** 70 Marks Theory + 30 Marks Practical & Viva Voce.
- **Subjects with Project Work (Mathematics, Accountancy, Economics, Business Studies, History, Political Science):** 80 Marks Theory + 20 Marks Internal Project Assessment.

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

c7033306-7665-4eea-9c2f-b04d6ca0520d.text:
## 4. Passing and Promotion Criteria
- To pass a subject, a student must secure a minimum of **33% marks overall**, as well as **33% separately in both Theory and Practical/Internal assessments**.
- **Compartment / Re-test Policy:** Students failing in up to two subjects in the Annual Examination are eligible to appear for a Compartment Examination held within 15 days of result declaration. Students failing in three or more subjects will be detained in the same grade.

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

ea18c007-52bd-41df-b852-e565e5029665.text:
## 5. 8-Point Scholastic Grading Scale
- **A1 (91% – 100%):** Outstanding
- **A2 (81% – 90%):** Excellent
- **B1 (71% – 80%):** Very Good
- **B2 (61% – 70%):** Good
- **C1 (51% – 60%):** Above Average
- **C2 (41% – 50%):** Average
- **D (33% – 40%):** Marginal (Pass)
- **E (Below 33%):** Essential Repeat / Needs Improvement

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

addfdc44-8089-4f3c-8718-5ec2b368a3dd.text:
## 6. Examination Conduct and Unfair Means
- Electronic calculators, mobile phones, smartwatches, and written notes are strictly barred inside the examination hall.
- Any student caught using unfair means will have their answer script canceled immediately and will be awarded zero marks in that subject.

metadata.title: Examination Framework, Assessment Pattern, and Promotion Rules

9d6e0168-3a8e-40b9-b350-faf648eed2fa.text:
# SCHOOL BUS TRANSPORT AND CENTRAL LIBRARY REGULATIONS

## 1. School Transport Service and Fee Slabs
The school operates GPS-enabled, CCTV-monitored buses staffed with a trained driver, conductor, and a female bus attendant on every route. Transport fees are billed quarterly along with tuition fees:
- **Zone A (Up to 5 km from campus):** ₹1,800 per month (₹5,400 per quarter).
- **Zone B (5.1 km to 12 km from campus):** ₹2,400 per month (₹7,200 per quarter).
- **Zone C (12.1 km to 20 km from campus):** ₹3,000 per month (₹9,000 per quarter).

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations

4ff8758b-c5ee-48b3-8f73-df6731dedcdb.text:
## 2. Bus Boarding, Safety, and Route Rules
- **Stop Arrival:** Students must reach their designated pickup stop at least 5 minutes prior to the scheduled arrival time. Buses will not wait for latecomers.
- **Discontinuation / Route Change:** Transport facility is opted for a full term. Parents wishing to discontinue or change a bus stop must submit a written application to the Transport In-Charge at least 15 days before the start of a new quarter.

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations

c34f5576-76e3-40fb-a8b0-c0a6869f2550.text: - **Bus Discipline:** Students must remain seated with seatbelts fastened while the bus is in motion. Leaning out of windows, shouting, or eating inside the bus is prohibited.

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations

7c184bc9-3a22-4a4d-aeb6-b4e85297f625.text:
## 3. Central Library Timings and Membership
- **Operating Hours:** 8:00 AM to 3:30 PM on all working days (Monday to Saturday).
- **Membership:** All enrolled students and faculty members are automatic members of the Central Library using their School ID card barcode.

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations

18f6aa9b-b702-49ed-ab05-7910de1477bc.text:
## 4. Book Borrowing Limits and Loan Duration
- **Grades 1 to 5:** Maximum of 1 fiction/story book for 7 days.
- **Grades 6 to 10:** Maximum of 2 books (1 academic reference + 1 general/fiction) for 14 days.
- **Grades 11 & 12:** Maximum of 3 books for 14 days, plus access to the competitive exam reference section.
- **Non-Issuable Items:** Encyclopedias, dictionaries, current periodicals, and rare reference volumes are for in-library reading only.

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations

5dadbd77-24df-48f5-b3ff-5770d0fa30c6.text:
## 5. Overdue Fines and Damaged Books
- **Late Return Fine:** ₹5 per book per working day after the due date. Borrowing privileges are temporarily suspended until overdue books are returned and fines are cleared.
- **Lost or Damaged Books:** Highlighting, underlining, tearing pages, or losing a library book requires the student to either replace the book with a brand-new copy of the exact same edition or pay the full current market price plus a ₹100 processing fee.

metadata.title: School Bus Transport and Central Library Regulations
